cohort: The study included 30 pregnant women diagnosed with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE), predominantly aged 18-35 and 80% nulliparous, with a mean SLE disease duration of 3.93 years.
finding: The study found that pregnancies in women with SLE were associated with a high incidence of complications, including preterm labor (26.67%), missed abortion (10%), preeclampsia (6.67%), and intrauterine death (10%).
mod_finding: Delivery was most frequently by cesarean section (70%).
gest_age: 26.67% of cases involved preterm labor; 73.33% of patients were admitted after reaching 37 weeks of gestation.
